3-1.question: Which of these are true about the dealer (East)?
options: Takes the first turn of the hand
Keeps the deal after a washout
3-1.explanation: East starts with 14 tiles and discards first, while a washout still passes the deal on and the dealer gets no scoring bonus.

3-1.question: How many rounds does a full game have?
3-1.explanation: A full game runs four rounds: East, South, West and North.

3-1.question: Match each setup step with what it decides.

pairs.right: The deal still passes to the next player

3-1.explanation: The dice only pick the break point, the wind draw fixes seats, and a washout rotates the deal.

3-1.question: Rounds run East, South, West, North. Which Wind tile marks the second round?
3-1.explanation: The South round is the second of the four rounds.

3-1.question: Arrange the Wind tiles in seating order, starting from the dealer.
3-1.explanation: Seats and turns run counter-clockwise: East, South, West, North.

3-2.question: Which statements about the deal are correct?
options: Tiles are taken four at a time
Players go three times round before the single tile
Flowers are kept hidden in the hand
3-2.explanation: The deal is four tiles three times round plus one each, the dealer holds 14, and flowers are shown.

3-2.question: How many times does the deal go round taking four tiles?
3-2.explanation: Three passes of four tiles give everyone 12 before the single tile.

3-2.question: Match each situation with what happens.

pairs.right: Show it and draw a replacement
You wait with 13 tiles for your first draw

3-2.explanation: Flowers leave the hand immediately, and only East begins by discarding because East already holds 14 tiles.

3-2.question: Which of these must be declared face-up and replaced?
3-2.explanation: Flower tiles are declared and replaced; the other three stay in your hand.

3-2.question: Where does a replacement tile for a Flower come from?
3-2.explanation: Flower replacements are drawn from the back (end) of the wall.

3-3.question: Which are true during a normal turn?
options: You draw one tile from the wall
You may discard two tiles instead
3-3.explanation: A turn is draw one, hold 14, then discard exactly one.

3-3.question: You hold 14 tiles after drawing. How many must you discard?
3-3.explanation: Discarding one tile returns your hand to 13.

3-3.question: Match each situation with what you do.

pairs.left: You draw a tile you cannot use
pairs.right: Discard it at the end of your turn
Declare the win instead of discarding
The hand ends in a washout

3-3.explanation: Drawing never forces a discard when you can win, and a Kong adds a replacement draw to the turn.

3-3.question: East has just discarded. Whose turn is next?
3-3.explanation: Turns pass counter-clockwise, so South plays after East.

3-3.question: Where are your discards placed?
options: Face-up in front of you, in order
3-3.explanation: Every player keeps a face-up row of discards, which is public information.

3-4.question: Which conditions must be met to call Chow?
options: You hold two suited tiles that complete a run
The discard comes from the player on your left
The completed run is three consecutive tiles of one suit
Any player at the table may feed your Chow
3-4.explanation: A Chow is a suited run fed only by the player immediately before you.

3-4.question: You hold {{m4}}{{m5}}. Which discard completes a Chow?
3-4.explanation: {{m3}}{{m4}}{{m5}} is a run, while {{m7}} would need a {{m6}} you do not hold.

3-4.question: Arrange these tiles into a Chow that uses your {{m3}} and {{m5}}.
3-4.explanation: {{m3}}{{m4}}{{m5}} is three consecutive tiles in one suit.

3-4.question: How many tiles do you reveal when you call Chow?
3-4.explanation: A Chow is a three-tile run shown face-up with the claimed discard.

3-4.question: Match the two tiles you hold with the discard you need for a Chow.
3-4.explanation: A run stays inside 1 to 9 in one suit, so 8-9 takes only 7, 1-2 takes only 3, and honour tiles cannot be chowed.

3-5.question: Which are true about a Pong?
options: You may claim it from any player
It beats a Chow for the same discard
You discard one tile after revealing it
It gives you a replacement draw from the back of the wall
3-5.explanation: Pong comes from any seat and outranks Chow; the replacement draw belongs to Kong.

3-5.question: You hold {{s7}}{{s7}}. Which discard completes a Pong?
3-5.explanation: A Pong needs the identical tile; {{s6}} or {{s8}} would make a Chow and {{p7}} is another suit.

3-5.question: Match what you hold with the claim it allows.

pairs.left: Two tiles one apart in one suit
Four melds and a pair worth 3+ faan

3-5.explanation: Each claim is defined by how many tiles you already hold and whether they match or run.

3-5.question: After calling Pong, how many tiles must you discard?
3-5.explanation: Claiming takes you to 14 tiles, so one discard brings you back to 13.

3-5.question: After your Pong, who plays next?
3-5.explanation: Play resumes from your seat, skipping the players in between.

3-6.question: Which of these are ways to make a Kong?
options: Claim a discard while holding three identical tiles
Draw all four identical tiles yourself
Add the fourth tile to an existing Pong
Claim a discard that matches two tiles in your hand
3-6.explanation: The three Kong types are exposed, concealed and supplemental, while two matching tiles are only a Pong.

3-6.question: How many identical tiles make a Kong?
3-6.explanation: A Kong is a meld of four identical tiles.

3-6.question: Match each Kong type with how it is made.

pairs.right: Claim the fourth tile from a discard
Add the fourth tile to your Pong
Taken from the back of the wall

3-6.explanation: The three kinds differ in where the fourth tile comes from, and all of them take a replacement from the wall's end.

3-6.question: You hold {{red}}{{red}}{{red}}. Which discard may you Kong?
3-6.explanation: A Kong needs the fourth copy of the identical tile.

3-6.question: Why do you draw a replacement after declaring a Kong?
options: The Kong takes four tiles into one meld
The dealer awards a free tile
The wall owes you a Flower
You must replace the tile you discarded
3-6.explanation: Four tiles become one meld, so the replacement keeps your hand at full size.

3-7.question: Which of these are valid ways to win?
options: Drawing your winning tile from the wall
Claiming a discard that completes your hand
Claiming any discard that completes a pair
3-7.explanation: You win by self-draw or by claiming a discard, and only with 3 faan or more.

3-7.question: What is the faan cap, however big the hand?
3-7.explanation: Every hand counts as at most 10 faan under these rules.

3-7.question: Match how the hand ends with who pays.

pairs.right: The discarder pays the full value
Each of the other three pays half value

3-7.explanation: 半銃制 means the discarder pays in full, while a self-draw is split in half across the three other players.

3-7.question: You hold {{m1}}{{m2}} and need one tile to win. Which discard completes your run?
3-7.explanation: {{m1}}{{m2}} waits only on {{m3}}, because a run cannot wrap past 9.

3-7.question: You self-draw a 4-faan hand. How much do you collect in total?
3-7.explanation: At 4 faan a discard win pays 16, so self-draw pays each player 8 for 24 in total.

3-8.question: Which claims may you make from any player's discard?
3-8.explanation: Only Chow is limited to the player on your left; the other claims may come from any seat.

3-8.question: Match each stage of the hand with its rule.

pairs.right: Draw one tile, then discard one
The replacement comes from the back of the wall

3-8.explanation: The flow runs deal, draw and discard, claim, then win or washout.

3-8.question: A discard win at 6 faan pays how many points?
3-8.explanation: The 半銃制 table pays 32 for a 6-faan discard win.

3-8.question: You hold {{p8}}{{p9}} and the player on your left discards. Which tile may you Chow?
3-8.explanation: {{p8}}{{p9}} waits only on {{p7}}, since a run cannot go past 9.

3-8.question: You need one tile for a 3-faan win; the player across needs the same tile for a Pong. Who gets it?
options: The player across, because Pong is a claim
You, because a win outranks every claim
3-8.explanation: A declared win beats Kong, Pong and Chow on the same discard.
